title: Reading — Words, Lines, and a First Passage
label: ch:sa-prathama-pathanam
canDo: I can read a Sanskrit word cold by looking at its ending first, see that three shuffles of one sentence are still one sentence, and hold a whole passage about one village without translating it word by word.

payoff.summary: Fourteen lines standing in one village, where च and वा follow what they join, किन्तु opens its line, and the whole thing closes on शान्तिः.
payoff.note: The reading rung is placed after the joiners of Chapter 52 rather than beside the deixis of Chapter 14, because a passage that can only place things is a list. च, वा and किन्तु are what turn fourteen lines into something held together, and all three were paid for before this chapter opens.
